problems.stem: A moderator logs: "Participant was confused and didn't understand the cart page." Why is this not usable observation data?
options: It is missing the participant's name.
It records the observer's inference (confused, didn't understand) instead of the observable behavior that another analyst could verify.
It is too short to be a valid note.
Observation notes should never mention specific pages.
problems.explanation: An observation protocol captures what was seen or heard; conclusions like 'confused' are inferences that belong in later analysis.

problems.stem: Which entry best follows a behavior-anchored observation protocol?
options: The navigation is obviously broken and frustrating.
01:42, settings page: participant clicked Back twice, said "where is the save button?", scrolled to bottom, then closed the tab.
Participant did not like the design.
This screen needs a complete redesign.
problems.explanation: A strong entry timestamps the moment, anchors to the screen, and records verbatim action and speech, not a verdict.

problems.stem: You use an AI transcription tool that also auto-labels each moment as "frustration" or "satisfaction." What is the defensible boundary?
options: Accept the AI emotion labels as your observation data.
Keep the AI transcript as a record of what was said, but treat the auto emotion labels as inferences to verify against observed behavior, not as data.
Disable transcription because all AI in observation is unreliable.
Use only the emotion labels and discard the transcript.
problems.explanation: AI can capture what was said, but inferred emotion labels are interpretations and must be checked against observable behavior before counting.

problems.stem: Two moderators run the same study but each free-writes notes in their own style. At analysis they cannot agree on how many participants hit a given problem. What protocol flaw caused this?
options: Without shared, predefined codes anchored to task steps, notes are not comparable, so the same event is counted inconsistently.
They should have recorded video instead of taking notes.
One moderator was simply more skilled than the other.
problems.explanation: A protocol needs predefined, shared observation categories so events are recorded and counted the same way across moderators.
